correctness.rationale: For A=uφ, B=vψ, a nonzero equality AB=BA forces their image lines to agree, whence φ(v)=ψ(u)=0, a contradiction. For every clique the image span W is nonzero and killed by every member. The image span and common kernel of the full canonical family at W both equal W, proving maximality and injectivity. For dimension r its size is [r]_q(q^(n−r)−1); minimizing q^r+q^(n−r) gives the middle dimensions. Maximal families through A correspond to all subspaces of ker(A)/im(A). For fixed W the tuple counts with image in U≤W hold with kernels required to contain W, not merely U; lattice inversion isolates exact spans and division by k! forgets order. This applies in characteristic two and to nonprime field orders. Independently built GF(2) matrices and exhaustive searches at n=3,4 verified the maximal families and counts through k=4; proof, not finite checks, gives the general result and remaining coefficients.
residual_risks: Independent finite enumeration used GF(2) and did not exhaust k>4. The Möbius formula covers those coefficients.
